title: Local span tagger, measured against both the rule tagger and a real pretrained NER on the exact fixture that motivated this todo
goal: If rule-tagger hard-slice F1 is too low, train a span tagger only on locally labeled spans. Verify the trigger condition still holds (it does: a real pretrained NER model does not fix it either, F1=0.4138 vs the rule tagger's 0.4615) before training anything, then measure whether a token-level classifier trained only on this repo's own labels actually helps.
method: Per-token multinomial logistic regression (sklearn), features from spaCy POS tags/token shape only (lab.common.rules._parser, never doc.ents -- no pretrained NER model used anywhere in this exploration). Trained on EXP-008's own EASY+HARD lines (every gold span already stored in this repository). Sentence-grouped GroupKFold cross-validation so no sentence's tokens appear in both train and test within a fold. Predicted spans reconstructed from contiguous same-label token runs, scored with EXP-008's own exact-span prf(), broken out by slice.
results_prose: Sentence-grouped 5-fold cross-validated local span tagger on 335 tokens from 52 sentences (EXP-008's own EASY+HARD fixture, nothing newly labeled): hard-slice exact-span F1=0.2105 (precision=0.2, recall=0.2222), easy-slice F1=0.2936. Baselines on the same hard sentences: rule tagger F1=0.4615 (EXP-008), real pretrained NER (dslim/bert-base-NER) F1=0.4138 (EXP-080) -- the local tagger does not improve on both.
conclusion: The local tagger did not clear both baselines on this fixture -- see metrics for the exact numbers, reported as measured rather than assumed to work. The fixture is tiny (10 hard sentences); a token-level classifier with only 5-fold sentence-grouped CV has very little signal to learn from.
scale_down: 10 hard sentences, 19 gold hard-slice spans total -- a genuinely small fixture for a trained classifier; this result should not be read as a general claim about span tagging, only about this specific repository's own fixture. Per-token classification with contiguous-run span reconstruction, not a true BIO/CRF sequence tagger -- adjacent same-label entities would merge into one span, a real limit not exercised by this particular fixture (no two adjacent gold spans share a label here) but not proven absent either.
models_used: Multinomial logistic regression (sklearn) trained only on labels already stored in this repository. spaCy en_core_web_sm's POS tagger (lab.common.rules._parser, already a dependency) for features -- its NER component is never read. No pretrained NER model, no generative model.
